# Module `http`

http - a pure-Vyb HTTP/1.1 server and client over the runtime sockets.

Everything here is written in Vyb on top of the `network` module - http uses
sockets but its own public surface stays just `http_*` functions carrying
`Int`s/Strings. No new FFI and no C code. It is minimal by design but real: it parses request
heads, builds well-formed responses, and serves and fetches over TCP
loopback/lan.

  Server (building blocks):
    http_listen(port, backlog) -> TcpListener?   open + bind + listen (0 = ephemeral)
    http_local_port(listener) -> Int             the bound port (handy after a 0)
    http_accept(listener) -> TcpStream?          accept one pending connection
    http_read_head(fd, max) -> String            read the head, up to CRLFCRLF
    http_request_path(head) -> String            "GET /x HTTP/1.1" -> "/x"
    http_send_all(fd, data) -> Int               send the whole string
    http_close(fd) -> Int                        close a socket/connection
    http_response(status, body) -> String        a well-formed text/plain response

  Client (convenience):
    http_request(method, path, host) -> String   a request head
    http_read_rest(fd, max) -> String            everything until the peer closes
    http_get(host, port, path) -> String?        full GET round-trip -> body (absent on failure)
    http_get_full(host, port, path) -> HttpResponse?  full HTTP/1.1 client

  Concurrent server:
    http_serve(port, backlog) -> TcpListener?  listen + accept on a worker thread
                                               (one detached thread per connection)

  Fallibility: absences above are failures. Escalate via `match`/`else`
  and `fail http_error(op, target)` into the fail/trap framework.

Threading: `http_serve` runs the accept loop on a worker thread and serves
each accepted connection on its own detached thread, so the server keeps
accepting while connections are handled concurrently (via the `threads`
module's `thread_spawn` / `thread_detach`). The sockets remain blocking, so
an accept only returns once the kernel has queued a connect. `http_get`
blocks until a *living* peer responds, so exercise it against an
external/local server.

<a id="sym-http_read_chunked"></a>
### `http_read_chunked` · fn

```
http_read_chunked(fd<Int>)<String> ->
```

Read the body of a `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` response from `fd`, draining
each hex chunk-size line, its data, and the trailing CRLF, until the 0-size
terminator and any trailer. Skipping the framing means the renderer no longer
sees stray hex sizes like "8000"/"464" as page text.

**Relationships**

- calls [`http_parse_hex`](#sym-http_parse_hex)

<a id="sym-http_read_line"></a>
### `http_read_line` · fn

```
http_read_line(fd<Int>)<String> ->
```

Read one CRLF-terminated line (without the CRLF) from `fd`. One byte is read
per iteration and the CRLF is located with index_of, so the reader stops
exactly at the line end without swallowing the header body.

<a id="sym-http_serve"></a>
### `http_serve` · fn

```
http_serve(port<Int>, backlog<Int>)<TcpListener?> ->
```

Start a threaded HTTP/1.1 server: bind+listen on `port` (0 = ephemeral; read
it back via http_local_port), spawn a detached worker running the accept
loop, and return the listener as a `TcpListener?` (absent on failure). Each
connection is served concurrently on its own detached thread via
http_serve_conn. The server stops once the listener is closed and the pending
accept returns an absent `TcpStream?` (the accept worker then reaps itself);
prefer closing when no connect is in flight.

**Relationships**

- calls [`http_accept`](#sym-http_accept)
- calls [`http_close`](#sym-http_close)
- calls [`http_listen`](#sym-http_listen)
- calls [`http_serve_conn`](#sym-http_serve_conn)

- calls [`thread_spawn`](threads.md#sym-thread_spawn)
- uses type [`TcpListener`](network.md#sym-tcplistener)

### `http_serve_conn` · fn

```
http_serve_conn(conn<TcpStream>)<Int> ->
```

Serve one accepted connection on a fresh detached thread: read its head,

closing. Runs concurrently with the rest of the server.

<a id="sym-httperror"></a>
### `HttpError` · struct

```
struct HttpError {
```

Fields:

- `op<String>`
- `target<String>`
- `message<String>`

A shared error value for escalating a failed HTTP op into the fail/trap
framework. `op` names the failing call ("get", "listen", "accept", ...);
`target` is the host:port (or port) intended; `message` is a fixed
description (http is pure Vyb, so there is no low-level diagnostic to
snapshot). Build with a literal or via `http_error()`.

**Relationships**

- mentions [`http_error`](#sym-http_error)

<a id="sym-httpresponse"></a>
### `HttpResponse` · struct

```
struct HttpResponse {
```

Fields:

- `status<Int>`
- `reason<String>`
- `headers<Vec<String>>`
- `body<String>`

A parsed HTTP response. `headers` holds the raw response header lines (minus
the terminating blank line); `body` is the payload (Content-Length-sized, or
everything read before the peer closed). `status` is -1 when no response could
be completed.

**Relationships**

- referenced by 1: [`https`](https.md)
